items.prompt: What process in stars makes heavier elements?

steps: Fusion joins nuclei into heavier elements.

items.prompt: What do stars first fuse hydrogen into?
Where are the heaviest elements made?

items.answer: The explosion of a large star

steps: A supernova is an exploding large star.

items.prompt: Can elements made in stars become part of planets?

steps: Spread elements become part of planets.

items.prompt: Where did the atoms in your body come from?

steps: Stars made the elements in your body.

items.prompt: Name a heavy element made in supernovas.

steps: Gold and uranium form in supernovas.

items.prompt: Can fusion make elements like carbon and oxygen?

steps: Fusion makes carbon and oxygen in stars.

items.prompt: Do new stars form from material enriched with heavy elements?

steps: New stars form from enriched material.

items.prompt: Do stars produce most of the elements?
Explain how heavy elements end up in new planets.
items.answer: Exploding stars spread heavy elements that become part of new planets

steps: Supernovas spread elements into new planets.

items.prompt: Why do we say the atoms in us were made in stars?
items.answer: Stars made the elements, which became part of living things

steps: Star-made elements became part of us.

items.prompt: How do supernovas differ from ordinary fusion in making elements?
items.answer: Supernovas make the heaviest elements, which ordinary fusion cannot

items.prompt: What happens to elements after a star makes them?

steps: Elements spread into space after being made.

items.prompt: Communicate how the universe's elements were produced.
items.answer: Stars make elements by fusion and supernovas make the heaviest, then they spread through space

steps: Fusion and supernovas produce and spread the elements.
